explanation: A bat's wing is skin stretched between very long finger bones, so it is really a hand. Flying squirrels, colugos and sugar gliders glide on skin flaps instead.

claims.text: Bats are capable of powered, flapping flight.
Flying squirrels, colugos and sugar gliders glide on skin membranes and cannot achieve powered flight.
A bat's wing is a membrane of skin stretched between greatly elongated finger bones.
